item.text:
Do not replace the current approach with the automated proposal.

On the supplied evidence, automation reduces staff time by 100 minutes but lowers correct first submissions from 90% to 65%—a 25-percentage-point decline and 3.5 times the error rate. That directly conflicts with your stated priority, so full automation is infeasible as posed.

Recommended direction: retain the current quality-controlled process and test automation only as an internal drafting or pre-check tool with mandatory staff review. Proceed only if a controlled comparison shows it maintains at least the current 90% correctness rate while reducing total staff time, including review and rework. If it cannot meet that quality floor, stop the automation path regardless of its time savings.
